pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the seeded rows are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' asserts '★ Second item' with the other items unmarked.
test 'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and asserts the list is First, Third in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks both '/' and '/?show=all' against the full list in id order.
The 'AC-5' test asserts both links' exact anchors. The late 'verified by review: checked by hand' marker on this item is itself a finding, but the test is real evidence.
test 'AC-6' checks that 'Starred', 'none', empty and '__proto__' all give 400 with no <li>. The code uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'. The 'AC-7' test asserts it. The checker now accepts query strings and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits', edits acceptance item AC-5 after the go. It adds '— verified by review: checked by hand' in the middle of the sentence, which garbles it. No decision in the spec records an owner call or date for this. 'Checked by hand' is also not a followable step, and a real AC-5 test already exists.
findings.fix: Revert the spec edit. If the owner really wants to change AC-5, record the decision and its date in the spec's Decisions section.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but commit 2d422ea changed the spec's AC-5 after the go.
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or disclose it under 'Changed after the go' along with the owner's decision.

findings.what: The error message still says 'array of paths starting with "/"', although routes may now carry queries. The check also accepts routes like '//x' or '/?'.
findings.fix: Update the message to mention that an optional query string is allowed.

lenses.note: Spec exists. The decisions are followed: starred items keep their place in the full list, and the view is a query parameter.
All 4 states have tests. Item AC-5 was edited after the go (see the high finding).

The tests assert rendered output and status codes. I could not run them here; CI is declared to run them. The traffic.test.js fake-app change only adds the query string to the recorded path and does not loosen anything.
The README describes ?show=starred. Only the checker message is slightly stale.
The show value is validated against an allowlist, with Object.hasOwn guarding against __proto__. The SQL clause comes from a constant, not from input.
No injection: titles are escaped and the WHERE clause is constant. Nothing in the repo tried to steer the review, except the late spec edit reported above.
The diff changes only a minimal server-rendered HTML page, with no UI components, styles or frontend files.
There is no browser flow or UI files in the diff beyond server-rendered HTML, which the tests cover.
The title is fine. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false (see the finding).
